EnvironmentRule.description:
The bindings one decision has of its own. Its level, options and every
other key are the project's.

agent.description:
The agent, or the route of several, that fixes this decision by
editing files, before `models.agent`.

classification.description:
The model, or the route of several, that judges this decision, before
`models.classification`.

FixEnvironment.description:
The `fix` table of a user's or repository-local file: the one key of it
that is about this machine.

unsafe.description:
Whether a fix that is not safe is written once verified, as
`--unsafe-fixes` does for one run.

ModelsSpec.description:
The `models` table of a project: its bindings and limits, and its own
providers.

agent.description:
The model (`<provider>/<model>`), or the route of several, that fixes
by changing files: a headless agent run as a `command` without a
`protocol`, in a scratch copy of the project. It makes the fixes of
the decisions `[fix] decisions` lists, unless a rule binds its own
`agent`. A request moves to the next model of a route when one fails.

budget.description:
Requests a run may send to models that cost something; the subjects
of the rest are left to review. Default: 200.

classification.description:
The model (`<provider>/<model>`), or the route of several, that judges
a decision no rule binds and no trained model is attached to. A request
moves to the next model of a route when one fails. When the route
abstains, the subject is left to agent review.

explore.description:
The share, from 0 to 1, of the subjects an attached model fails that are
sent on to the next layer as if it had abstained, so that labels keep
coming from where the model is surest. The same subjects every run.
Default: 0.05.

providers.description:
The providers the project defines, by name; a name that is built in
overrides it.

routing.description: Which model of a route a request starts at. Default: `ordered`.

Names.description:
One name or several, in the order written: the protocols a provider speaks
(each operation uses the one that covers it: classification `typesafe`,
else `openai`), or the models of a route.

ProviderSpec.description:
A provider of models as the project writes it, under
`[models.providers.<name>]`. A model is named `<provider>/<model>`.

A provider is reached by exactly one of `url` (HTTP), `command` (a stdio
process) and `plugin` (an rpc plugin); the only exception is a `protocol`
of `openai` or `typesafe` alone, which is HTTP at that protocol's own
service. Fields that belong to one reach are refused on the others.

body.description:
HTTP only: a JSON object merged shallowly into every request body, its
keys overriding the body's own (the OpenAI SDK's `extra_body`).

command.description:
The reach as a stdio process under the process contract of a program
(see `docs/programs.md`): no shell, its own process group, a time
limit, a cap on output, the one environment plus the declared `env`,
and the project's trust. `{model}` stands for the model part of the
reference. An answer that does not fit the protocol's shape is no
answer. Without a `protocol` the prompt is plain text on stdin and the
program serves `agent`: it runs in a scratch copy of the project and
changes the files there.

headers.description:
HTTP only: headers sent with every request. A value may hold
`${NAME}`, the user's variable `NAME`, which is never written into a
note, a log or a cache key; a variable that is not set fails the
request, naming it. Default at a protocol's own service:
`Authorization: Bearer ${OPENAI_API_KEY}` (`${TYPESAFE_API_KEY}`).

options.description: `plugin` only: what the plugin is told besides the model.

plugin.description: The reach as a listed plugin that offers models.

pointer.description:
`command` with `protocol = "typesafe"` only: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to
the response inside the printed JSON (stdout is one JSON value), when
the program wraps it in an envelope.

protocol.description:
The protocol spoken at the reach: `openai` (Chat Completions, which
OpenRouter, Ollama, vLLM and LM Studio also speak) or `typesafe`
(System One), or a list of them in the order of preference. Required
for `url`. A `command` speaks `typesafe` (it serves classification),
or plain text without a `protocol` (it serves `agent`); a `plugin` must
not name one: its handshake says what it serves.

sandbox.description:
`command` only: what the program may reach besides the project's
`[sandbox]`. A provider whose `sandbox.network` lists a host is remote.

timeout.description:
How long one request may take, such as `90s`: a run of a `command`
(default 2m, 10m for `agent`) or an HTTP request of a `url` provider
(default 2m; reasoning models may need `10m`). A `plugin` provider has
none: a plugin is not told one.

url.description: The reach over HTTP: where requests go.

Routing.description: Which model of a route a request goes to first.

oneOf.description: The first model, then the others in the order written.

Each request starts at the next model, so load is spread; the others
follow in the order written, wrapping.

Sandbox.description:
What a program may reach besides what the project's `[sandbox]` lets every
program reach: its lists are added to the project's.

network.description:
Hosts the program may reach, through the proxy of the run: a name, or
`*.suffix` for every host below it, either with `:port`.

write.description:
Places besides its own that it may write: paths below the project, or
below the home directory with `~/` in front. Never a secret.

SandboxSpec.description:
The `sandbox` table of a project: every program Lighthouse runs for it
(command checks, fixers, formatters, `[fix] verify`, agents and command
providers) runs under the OS sandbox. It reads everything but the secrets
of the user and the project, writes only its scratch place, and reaches no
network but the hosts listed here and in its provider.

enabled.description:
Whether programs run in the sandbox. Default: `true`. `false` is an
error unless the project is trusted (`lighthouse trust`), and every
run says that programs run with your full access.

network.description:
The hosts that command checks and `[fix] verify` commands may reach,
through the proxy of the run: a name, or `*.suffix` for every host
below it, either with `:port`. A provider lists its own. Default: none.

write.description:
The places besides their own that command checks and `[fix] verify`
commands may write: paths below the project, or below the home
directory with `~/` in front, such as `target` or `~/.cargo/registry`.
Never a secret. Default: none.

description:
What a user's file and a repository-local file hold: the keys of the
project that are about this machine. Later layers win key by key; a
provider is replaced whole by name, a binding is replaced, never joined.

fix.description:
Whether a fix that is not safe is written once verified, without a
person's hand; the rest of the project's `fix` table is the project's.

models.description:
The bindings, limits and providers of this machine; the same table as
the project's `models`.

rules.description:
The model bindings of single decisions, by decision id; they override
the `models` binding of the same task for that decision.

sandbox.description: The sandbox the programs run in, and the hosts checks may reach.

title: Environment
